answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism. In this setup, each new identity incurs a debt to their inviter for every downstream identity created For instance, if an inviter spawns five identities, their total debt can reach 500 tokens. Each identity must also provide unique, verifiable contributions, acting as a beacon amidst a lagoon of creativity. If the inviter's debt surpasses their stake, they forfeit their balance. This makes the creation of fake identities costly, much like attempting to write with a quill when the ink runs dry.
